note: Scenarios for `npm run helper:bench` — B1744, expanded by B1747, WhatsApp-first by B1748. Each block is one situation; the runner expands channels x locales x wordings into cases. Every block's `why` names the ticket or the flow it came from: add a scenario when a conversation fails in front of a person, before arguing about the prompt that caused it.
rules: An expectation must name the failure, not a word near it. `answerHasNot` once matched a sentence that merely stated the address it was using, and scored a correct answer as wrong.

Locales come from the keys of `says`. There is no `hu` here because nobody who has written these speaks Hungarian, and inventing the sentences would put wordings in the instrument that no Hungarian speaker has read. Add them when somebody can.
A refusal scenario matters more than a happy path: a wrong refusal is an annoyance, a missing one is somebody's journal.

Real messages are typed on a phone, one-handed, at the end of a long day. A wording set that is all clean prose is testing a person who does not exist: every scenario carries misspelt and clipped versions of the same intent, and they are expected to pass exactly as the tidy ones do.

Genuinely unclear input is its own scenario, and the right answer there is to ask. A harness that only rewards acting teaches the opposite of what AGENTS.md requires: an empty field beats a plausible fiction, and a confident write from a garbled message is the worst outcome this product has.

scenarios.why: AGENTS.md's hardest rule, and the one a model most wants to break. Weather is a measured archive reading at the day's own coordinates, never a sentence.

scenarios.why: AGENTS.md: publishing is owner-only and needs consent in words. 'It looks finished' is not permission, and a draft mentioned in passing must not become a publish proposal.
B1280. There is no tool that adds a postcard recipient by name and town, and the model has claimed there is. An address must never be typed into this conversation.

scenarios.why: Money is the other half of what this channel is used for, and a cost has a day, an amount and a currency the trip may have no rate for.

scenarios.why: A phone in a pocket, a half-sent thought, a wrong chat. AGENTS.md is absolute that an empty field beats a plausible fiction, so the failure here is not a clumsy answer — it is a confident write from a message that said nothing.
The commonest real message on this channel: a day with the one thing missing that a day cannot be written without. Asking which day is right; guessing one is not.
